description: Me apasiona la ciencia, la exploración espacial y comprender cómo se comporta la combustión en condiciones de microgravedad. Nuestro proyecto, Flame in Freefall: Análisis de seguridad contra incendios mediante inteligencia artificial y datos de combustión en microgravedad, busca explorar cómo la inteligencia artificial y el análisis de datos pueden ayudarnos a comprender mejor el comportamiento del fuego y mejorar la seguridad en el espacio.
summary: Project Yicra is an interactive, AI-powered web dashboard designed to consolidate, classify, and interpret NASA’s microgravity and reduced-gravity fire safety research. Built using a standardized JSON data architecture, the platform integrates empirical findings from NASA’s Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository and Glenn Research Center campaigns—including PSI-62 (concurrent flame spread), SoFIE (solid fuel ignition and extinction), FLARE (reduced-gravity flammability limits), FM2 (lunar combustion), and SAME (smoke aerosol measurements). By combining dynamic fuel and gravity-regime filtering, comparative Earth-versus-space visualizations, cabin fire-risk simulations, and an integrated AI interpreter, Project Yicra transforms fragmented experimental records into actionable engineering insights. This solution directly addresses the challenge of making complex space combustion data accessible and operational, helping mission planners and spacecraft engineers select safer materials, improve early fire detection, and protect crews during future Artemis lunar and Mars exploration missions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:
Project Yicra is an interactive web intelligence dashboard built around a modular, standardized JSON schema that unifies experimental data from NASA’s combustion science programs—specifically PSI-62, SoFIE, FLARE, FM2, and SAME—alongside historical spacecraft fire-detection insights. Users can dynamically load experimental records, filter datasets by material/fuel classification, gravity regime (microgravity, lunar 1/6g, reduced-g, and Earth 1g), or hazard level, and compare flame-spread and smoke-aerosol behaviors across environments. It also features a cabin fire-risk interpreter and an AI assistant that translates dense scientific parameters into clear executive summaries and safety assessments.

Benefits & Intended Impact:
El comportamiento del fuego de las naves espaciales difiere drásticamente de los incendios terrestres porque la ausencia de convección impulsada por la flotabilidad altera la geometría de las llamas, los umbrales de ignición y el tamaño de las partículas de humo. Al centralizar los conjuntos de datos dispersos del PSI y del Centro de Investigación Glenn de la NASA en una única interfaz visual,el Proyecto Yicra reduce el tiempo de búsqueda de la investigación y evita la aplicación incorrecta de los estándares de inflamabilidad terrestre de 1g en los hábitats espaciales, y apoya una selección de materiales más segura y una calibración de detectores de alerta temprana para las operaciones de la ISS, los hábitats lunares de Artemis y los vehículos de tránsito del espacio profundo.

Tools, Languages & Software Used:
- Frontend & UI: HTML5, Tailwind CSS, and vanilla JavaScript for responsive, zero-dependency client-side rendering and interactive filtering.
- Data Architecture: Standardized JSON schemas structured from official NASA PSI repositories and NASA Glenn Combustion Science documentation.
- AI & Prototyping: Google Gemini (Large Language Model) for data structuring, scientific synthesis, code scaffolding, and interactive dashboard prototyping.

Creativity:
The project is named after "Yicrá," a traditional woven bag from Costa Rica’s indigenous Brunca culture used to gather and carry essential tools and provisions. Reflecting that concept, Project Yicra weaves together scattered, complex microgravity combustion experiments into a single, portable digital toolkit. Rather than displaying static tables, it pairs comparative 1g-vs-microgravity analytics with an AI safety interpreter designed for rapid engineering decision-making.

Key Factors Considered:
Our design prioritized data fidelity to primary NASA sources, strict separation between terrestrial (1g) and reduced-gravity combustion physics, extensibility (allowing new JSON investigation files to be imported seamlessly), and clean visual hierarchy so users can move from high-level executive summaries down to specific experimental metrics without cognitive overload.
